text:
Lara: Heads-up, shipping lane sync. we have a customer commitment window next week; need final GA checklist and a short public FAQ. goal: greenlight review Friday 09:00.
Mike: SLA numbers proposal: 99.95% monthly availability for hosted API, separate SLA for Dedicated with 99.99%. performance SLOs by model class (latency-optimized <=200ms p99, general <=350ms p99). open to adjustments.
Sasha: pricing approach: introduce three tiers (dev, reserved, enterprise). dev = metered hosted with burst caps, reserved = discounted commit, enterprise = custom. do we allow provisional pricing for GA with "subject to adjustment" note?
Lara: provisional ok if we lock the example scenarios and billing calc. customers must not see shifting numbers in week 1.
Nina: docs plan: quickstart, SLA one-pager, runbook excerpt (incident steps + communication templates), and a short "what to expect" FAQ for customers. I'll draft templates for escalations.
Raj: monitoring/ops: external uptime checks, synthetic traffic for common routes, per-model latency heatmap, and error-rate alerts. propose alert thresholds: 5xx >0.5% sustained for 5m, latency p99 > target for 3m. also add cache-hitrate drop >10% alert.
Lara: also include rollback decision criteria in runbook: % errors in last 5m, queue backlog growth, and degradation in customer-facing latency. add to playbook.
Mike: legal: service credit formula draft: credit = min(30% monthly invoice, (downtime_minutes / total_minutes) * monthly_fee). exceptions: customer misuse, planned maintenance with notice. @Legal can you confirm language?
Legal: will review and provide safe language. we prefer cap at 25% but can accept 30% with product signoff.
Sasha: examples needed for finance: 3 customer bills (1M tokens/mo, 5M tokens bursty, enterprise steady 50M). I'll post spreadsheets.
Nina: sample alert snippet for runbook (will paste into doc):
```
alert: LatencySpike
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/completions"}[5m])) by (le)) > 0.35
for: 3m
runbook: |
  - check recent deploys: `kubectl -n inference rollout status deploy/api`
  - validate queue lengths: `redwoodctl queue top`
  - if p99 above SLA and errors rising, trigger rollback via `deploy rollback --to stable` and notify #release-ops
```
Raj: I'll wire dashboards and attach alert links. also adding an entry: Dedicated customers get a separate pager and `#dedicated-ops` channel + a playbook to escalate to infra-oncall.
Lara: decision rule for GA: all four artifacts must be present and reviewed (SLA doc, pricing examples, runbook + playbooks, monitoring dashboards) AND smoke tests must pass. if any item missing, abort greenlight.
Mike: owners: SLA -> Mike, Pricing/finance examples -> Sasha, Docs/runbook -> Nina, Monitoring/alerts -> Raj, Legal text -> Legal. target drafts by Thu EOD for internal review.
Sasha: noted. will sync with finance and post examples by Thu noon.
Legal: I'll aim to have redlines by Thu EOD.
Deploy Bot: smoke tests kicked off by @ci at 2026-03-23T15:10:04Z. 5/6 smoke checks passed.
Nina: I'll open the PR for the runbook and link here when ready. includes customer-facing incident email templates.
Lara: communication: customer announcement copy must be reviewed by PM and Legal. keep messaging clear about "provisional pricing" if used.
Mike: quick checklist to include in SLA doc: scope, model class mapping, availability targets, credits calc, exclusions, how Dedicated SLAs differ, support response windows.
Raj: adding oncall playbook steps to the runbook: initial triage -> mitigation (failover, model variant) -> rollback -> customer comms -> RCA.
Lara: good. we'll meet Friday 09:00 to greenlight. if PRs not ready, we move to next week. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
